content.content: The reviewer reads the dependent's recorded account of how a state change is applied to the rendered surface and applies these criteria to it. (1) Use: the account claims that applying one change costs the same regardless of how many nodes and edges are rendered, and locates that saving in work that follows what the change affects. Fail if the account instead rests the claim on a frame-rate target, a latency budget, an event-rate ceiling, or a batching step whose saving is not tied to which elements changed: those substitute a goal for the bound and do not entail it. (2) Reachability: the elements a change affects are obtained from something the mechanism maintains about the surface (an element index, cached node/adjacency maps), not derived by reading or rebuilding the rendered surface. Fail if obtaining the affected set, or deciding whether to act, walks or queries every rendered node or edge. (3) Write scope: the change is applied only to the elements it affects. Fail on any step that writes, re-renders, re-classes or re-queries the whole surface when the change affects a subset, including a whole-surface step that appears on the normal path or as a fallback. (4) Per-event work: fail if any step taken per incoming change, before or during coalescing, does work proportional to the number of rendered nodes or edges, including computing a diff against the whole surface to discover what changed. (5) Coalescing: when several changes land within one frame, the surface is updated at most once per frame, and the coalescing is by merging pending changes rather than by dropping them; fail if correctness of the applied result depends on changes being discarded. (6) Consistency: fail on any element of the account that asserts or requires cost to grow with the number of rendered nodes or edges, on any path, since that contradicts the prerequisite. (7) Cost ownership: the account must cover the full cost of applying the change, from the arriving change through to what the surface ends up showing, or else state which part of that cost it leaves out and name a recorded decision that owns it — a decision that itself depends on the same prerequisite and assigns the cost of presenting the surface. Fail if any per-visible-node or per-visible-edge term in that full cost is neither covered by the account nor assigned to such a recorded decision, or if the account scopes itself to its own steps while the surface update it hands off to is described by no recorded decision. This criterion demands no rendering technique and fixes no layer of the cost to a particular owner; it demands only that no unowned per-visible-node term remain. The visible extent used in the check is whatever the surface renders at the time; the reviewer names the failing step or unowned term in the check's output.
content.rationale: The dependent records prose stating how an interaction applies state changes, and the prerequisite records prose stating that an interaction's cost follows what it changed rather than how many nodes are visible; both endpoints sit at the natural layer, so the matrix's natural-to-natural cell applies and the gate form's non-violation check is the base. The prerequisite's content is a cost relation, so non-violation cannot be settled by clause comparison alone: the criterion instantiates the prerequisite's own refuting observation against the dependent's described mechanism, asking whether applying the same change at different visible extents would do different work. That is why the criteria are structural rather than a mere licence check: they require the mechanism's work to reach only the affected elements, to avoid any whole-surface step on the normal path, and to coalesce per frame without paying per-event cost proportional to the surface, while refusing arguments that trade the bound for a frame-rate, latency or event-rate target or for a batching trick with no tie to what changed. An account can satisfy those steps and still leave the surface's own per-visible-node work outside what it records — and a scope that ends before the surface update is where a per-visible-node term survives unnoticed. The cost-ownership criterion therefore makes the accounting complete: the account either carries the whole cost or names the recorded decision that owns the part it leaves out, so a per-visible-node term can be owned or absent but not unaccounted for. It stays within the prerequisite, which bounds the interaction's cost rather than prescribing how the surface is presented, and it asserts nothing about whether the dependent or that other decision is implemented, so it survives rewording and rescoping of the account. The order of elements, the wording of the account and any particular data structure or rendering technique are not criteria; an account phrased or built differently passes provided each criterion holds of what it describes, and the failing step, unowned term or unnamed owner is named only in the check's output.
